summary: Assigns a value for EdDSA public keys in the IANA registry of IPSECKEY resource record parameters. This lets such keys be published in the DNS for IPsec use.

plainLanguage.summary: The address book has a list of key types it knows about. This adds one more type to that list.

questions: how to publish eddsa keys for ipsec in dns
subtitle: Registers a value so EdDSA public keys can be stored in IPSECKEY DNS records.

tldr.problem: The IPSECKEY DNS record stores public keys for IPsec, but its Algorithm Type registry had no entry for EdDSA keys.
tldr.mechanism: The document assigns algorithm value 4 to an EdDSA public key, formatted as in Section 3 of RFC 8080, and reformats the registry to add a Format Description column.
tldr.outcome: EdDSA public keys can be published in IPSECKEY records. The document adds no new security considerations.

today: RFC 9373 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: IPSECKEY and EdDSA
sections.content:
The IPSECKEY resource record (RFC 4025) stores public keys for IPsec systems in the DNS. It relies on the IANA "Algorithm Type Field" registry to list the permitted key formats.

This document adds EdDSA public keys, in the format defined in RFC 8080, to that list.
sections.plainLanguage: A DNS record can hold a key for secure connections. This says the new kind of key is allowed in it.

sections.title: Algorithm Value 4
sections.content:
When an EdDSA public key is put in an IPSECKEY record, the algorithm value 4 is used and the key is formatted as in Section 3 of RFC 8080. The registry entry reads "An EdDSA Public Key".

IANA also added a Format Description field to the registry and updated existing descriptions to say they are for "Public" keys. Existing values are 0 (no public key present), 1 (DSA), 2 (RSA) and 3 (ECDSA).
sections.plainLanguage: The list of key types now has a number 4 for the new kind, and a new column saying where its format is described.

sections.title: Example and Security
sections.content:
An appendix shows an IPSECKEY record with no gateway and an EdDSA public key in base64 presentation format, plus the matching private key in hex.

The security considerations of RFC 4025 apply, and the document introduces no new ones.
sections.plainLanguage: The document shows a sample entry, and says this change makes nothing less safe.

items.label: EdDSA
items.desc: An EdDSA public key, formatted as in RFC 8080, Section 3.

references.text: Richardson, M., "A Method for Storing IPsec Keying Material in DNS", RFC 4025, March 2005.
